# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Children with KBG syndrome may experience respiratory issues, such as recurrent ear infections and temporary loss of smell (anosmia), which can lead to breathing difficulties and reduced exercise tolerance.
    
## 2) CARDIOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Children with KBG syndrome are at an increased risk of congenital heart defects, specifically valve abnormalities and septal defects. While most do not develop serious heart conditions, some may experience transient episodes of congestive heart failure (CHF) or require pacemaker implantation.
    
## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Children with KBG syndrome commonly experience feeding difficulties, including reflux, poor suck-swallow-breathe coordination, and aspiration pneumonia. These issues can contribute to nutritional deficiencies and prolonged hospitalization.
    
## 4) IMMUNOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Individuals with KBG syndrome are at an increased risk of developing autoimmune diseases, such as Type 1 diabetes mellitus, Hashimoto’s thyroiditis, and autoimmune gastritis. Management strategies include dietary modifications, vitamin D supplementation, and immunomodulatory therapies.
    
## 5) NEUROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Children with KBG syndrome frequently exhibit developmental delays, behavioral differences, and sensorineural hearing loss. Neurological evaluations should include assessments of cognitive function, reflexes, and coordination.
    
## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Children with KBG syndrome are prone to recurrent otitis media (middle ear infections) and glue ear (fluid in the ear), leading to conductive hearing loss and potential speech delays. Regular ENT consultations are recommended.
    
## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Vision-related concerns in KBG syndrome include refractive errors (hyperopia, myopia, astigmatism), strabismus (eye misalignment), and presbyopia (difficulty reading close-up). Regular ophthalmological examinations are essential.
    
## 8) DERMATOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Individuals with KBG syndrome may display eczema-like skin conditions, including dry, itchy patches, and areas of thickened skin. Skin care routines and barrier protection are crucial.
    
## 9) DENTAL

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Teeth characteristics, such as macrodontia (large molars), brachydactyly (short fingers), and clinodactyly (curved fifth digit), can impact dental health. Orthodontic interventions may be necessary.
    
## 10) EDUCATION

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Academic achievement can vary widely. Some children excel in traditional classroom settings, while others require additional support in mainstream environments. Special educational provision (such as EHCP) may be beneficial.
    
## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Behavioural differences, including autism spectrum traits, anxiety, and executive function challenges, can influence social interactions and academic performance. Early identification and targeted interventions are critical.
    
## 12) SKELETAL

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Anomalies such as brachydactyly (short fingers) and clinodactyly (curved fifth finger) can impact dexterity and comfort during play and self-care tasks. Orthopedic evaluation and consideration of splints or braces may be warranted.
    
## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Screening:
    - Regular dental check-ups and orthodontic evaluations.
    - Monitoring for cardiovascular issues, including echocardiograms and ECGs.
    - Periodic review for cranial vault measurements (skull size) and hip circumference measurements.
    - Review for tethered cord syndrome (MRI).

b) Treatments:
    - Speech therapy: Addressing communication and swallowing difficulties.
    - Occupational therapy: Enhancing fine motor skills and daily living abilities.
    - Physical therapy: Improving postural control and reducing fatigue.
    - Behavioral therapy: Managing behavioral and emotional challenges.
    - Epilepsy management: Ensuring proper seizure control with anticonvulsants.
    - Nutritional support: Considering supplements for vitamins D and B12, iron, and omega-3 fatty acids.
    - Hearing aid fitting: Addressing conductive hearing loss.
    - Vestibular rehabilitation: Addressing balance and coordination issues.
    - Cranial ultrasound: Evaluating brain structures for anomalies.
    - Genetic counseling: Discussing future reproductive options and carrier screening.
    - Immunotherapy: Considering vaccinations and managing autoimmune conditions.
    - Dental prophylaxis: Preventative measures against cavities and gum disease.
    - Orthodontics: Addressing bite and jaw alignment issues.
    - Cardiology: Regular follow-up and management of heart conditions.
    - Ophthalmology: Annual comprehensive eye exams and addressing vision concerns.
    - Dermatology: Routine skincare routine and barrier protection.
    - Education: Tailored curriculum and accommodations based on individual needs.
    - Social: Support groups and community resources for families dealing with similar conditions.
    - Family planning: Genetic testing and considerations for future pregnancies.

a) How this affects the patient:

- Children with KBG syndrome are at risk of congenital heart defects, particularly valve abnormalities. Regular echocardiograms and follow-up with a pediatric cardiologist are crucial for monitoring and managing any heart-related concerns.

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome commonly experience feeding difficulties and gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD). Management strategies such as gradual introduction of solid foods, dietary modifications, and antacid medications may alleviate symptoms.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Individuals with KBG syndrome are more susceptible to developing autoimmune diseases later in life. Monitoring for autoimmune markers and considering prophylactic immunomodulatory therapies might be beneficial.

## 5) NEUROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Neurodevelopmental outcomes in KBG syndrome are characterized by delays in reaching developmental milestones, such as crawling, walking, and potty training. Behavioral differences, including autism spectrum traits, are also frequent. Speech delays are relatively common, though many eventually acquire functional speech abilities.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome are prone to recurrent otitis media (middle ear infections) and adenoid hypertrophy, leading to blockage of the Eustachian tubes. Antibiotic treatments and positional drainage maneuvers can help manage these issues.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Vision problems are quite common in KBG syndrome, including near-sightedness (hypermetropic), far-sightedness (hypometropic), and astigmatism. Regular eye examinations are essential to monitor and address these issues.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Individuals with KBG syndrome may exhibit eczema-like skin conditions, including dry, itchy patches that can be stubborn to treat. Frequent bathing and gentle skincare routines are helpful in maintaining skin health.

## 9) DENTAL

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Teeth characteristics like enlarged central incisors (large molars) and brachydactyly (shortened fingers) are notable features. Dental care should focus on strengthening enamel, preventing cavities, and addressing loose teeth.

## 10) EDUCATION

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Academic achievement can vary widely among individuals with KBG syndrome. While many receive adequate support and attend mainstream schools, those with significant learning challenges may require additional educational interventions such as Individualized Education Programs (IEPs).

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT

a) How this affects the patient:
- Behavioural differences, including autism spectrum traits and attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), are common. Speech delays and auditory processing issues can contribute to communication challenges.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- The prevalence of behavioral and cognitive differences underscores the importance of early intervention programs and supportive environments.

## 12) SKELETAL

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Skeletal features such as brachydactyly (short fingers) and an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis) are observed. Regular orthopedic evaluations are advised.

### Screening Recommendations:
- Regular dental check-ups: Addressing potential issues like weak enamel and gum inflammation.
- Hearing screenings: Monitoring for sensorineural hearing loss and recurrent ear infections.
- Cardiac screening: Following the initial diagnostic visit, consider annual echocardiogram checks.
- Orthodontic evaluation: Considering braces or expansion appliances to correct bite issues.
- Palatal assessment: Reviewing the palate for possible speech and feeding concerns.

### Treatments Recommendations:
- Speech therapy: Continuously monitored and adjusted based on progress.
- Physical therapy: Enhancing muscle strength and coordination.
- Dietary modifications: Supporting proper nutrition and hydration.
- Antifungal treatments: Managing fungal infections, particularly in the sinuses.
- Vitamin D supplementation: Supporting overall immune function and bone density.
- Immunotherapy: Considering prophylactic measures against autoimmune reactions.
- Surgical considerations: Depending on the severity of heart conditions, consideration of pacemakers or valve replacements.

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Children with KBG syndrome are at an increased risk of congenital heart defects, specifically abnormalities of the aortic valve and the pulmonary artery. These can lead to various cardiovascular issues, including heart murmurs, arrhythmias, and potential heart failure.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Children with KBG syndrome commonly experience feeding difficulties and swallowing issues, leading to a preference for softer, smoother textures in their diet. They may also develop gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), characterized by regurgitation of swallowed air and food, and possible aspiration pneumonia.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Individuals with KBG syndrome are more susceptible to developing autoimmune diseases, particularly inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) and type 1 diabetes. They may also be at an increased risk of developing allergies and eczema.

## 5) NEUROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Children with KBG syndrome frequently exhibit developmental delays, behavioral differences, and learning difficulties. They may also display characteristics of autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). Coordination issues, such as tripping over feet or bumping into objects, are common due to variations in muscle tone and reflexes.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Children with KBG syndrome are prone to recurrent otitis media (ear infections), which can lead to complications such as sensorineural hearing loss and chronic ear drainage (ozena).

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Individuals with KBG syndrome are at an increased risk of strabismus (eye misalignment) and may require corrective lenses or surgery to address refractive errors and improve visual alignment.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Children with KBG syndrome may experience a variety of skin concerns, including eczema-like patches (ichthyosiform erythematoid reaction), hyperpigmentation, and alopecia (hair loss). Freckling (acneiform pigmentation) is also a noted feature.

## 9) DENTAL

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Children with KBG syndrome frequently encounter dental challenges, including difficulty chewing, weak tooth enamel, and the presence of supernumerary teeth (extra teeth). Orthodontic intervention may be necessary to correct bite issues.

## 10) EDUCATION

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Education outcomes for individuals with KBG syndrome vary widely. While many achieve success in mainstream settings, those with more significant learning difficulties may require additional support in the classroom. Special educational needs (SEN) assessments and provision should be considered based on the individual’s needs.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Behavioural differences, including autistic traits, hyperactivity, and anxiety, are common in individuals with KBG syndrome. Management strategies, such as behavior therapy and educational interventions, may be beneficial.

## 12) SKELETAL

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Skeletal features, such as brachydactyly (short fingers) and clinodactyly (curved fifth finger), can contribute to movement difficulties and cosmetic concerns. Monitoring for skeletal anomalies, such as scoliosis and hip dysplasia, is recommended.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Screening:
    - Regular dental check-ups should be conducted throughout childhood to prevent and manage issues related to weak enamel and orthodontic concerns.
    
b) Treatments:
    - Addressing feeding difficulties and ensuring proper nutrition is crucial. Feeding tubes may be necessary for infants and young children to ensure adequate intake.
    - Management of GERD involves dietary modifications, antacid medications, and, in severe cases, surgical intervention.
    - Anticonvulsants may be prescribed for seizure management.
    - Speech therapy and physical therapy should be considered to address communication and mobility issues.
    - Behavioral therapy may be beneficial for managing co-morbidities such as autism and ADHD.
    - Referral for cardiac evaluation and consideration of pacemaker placement for individuals with structural heart anomalies.
    - Referral for ENT (Ear, Nose, Throat) assessment for management of recurrent otitis media and auditory processing issues.
    - Consideration of orthodontic intervention for supernumerary teeth and malocclusion.
    - Genetic counseling and testing for family members may be advisable given the high likelihood of recurrence in unaffected family members.
    - Regular monitoring for skeletal anomalies, including hip radiographs and wrist X-rays, should be performed.
    - Periodic ophthalmological evaluations should be conducted to monitor for retinal degeneration and other ocular concerns.
    - Consideration of periodic cranial MRI scans to monitor for cerebellar vermis size (CVS) and brainstem size (BSV) measurements, which correlate with CVS and BSV measurements respectively. CVS and BSV measurements are key predictors of cognitive outcomes in KBG syndrome. These measures should be taken annually starting at age 3 months and continued until age 5 years.

Proper hygiene practices and timely antibiotic treatment can help prevent or reduce these complications.

## 2) CARDIOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Children with KBG syndrome are at an increased risk of congenital heart defects, particularly valve abnormalities. Regular cardiovascular assessments are recommended, especially in the first year of life, to detect and address potential issues early.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Children with KBG syndrome commonly experience feeding difficulties, including refusal to eat solids, vomiting, and regurgitation. These issues can contribute to nutritional deficiencies and delayed growth. Management strategies may include dietary modifications, behavioral therapies, and, in some cases, gastrostomy tubes for enteral nutrition.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Individuals with KBG syndrome are at an increased risk of developing autoimmune diseases, such as Type 1 diabetes, thyroid disorders, and inflammatory bowel disease. Regular immunological evaluations and consideration of prophylactic vaccinations are advised.

## 5) NEUROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Neurological features in KBG syndrome include developmental delays, learning difficulties, and behavioral differences. Speech delay, coordination issues, and sensory integration dysfunction are common. Management strategies may include physical therapy, occupational therapy, and behavioral interventions.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Children with KBG syndrome are prone to recurrent ear infections (otitis media) and glue ear (otocholemic maculopathy), which can lead to hearing loss and speech delays. Regular audiometric checks and timely intervention are crucial.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Vision-related concerns in KBG syndrome include refractive errors (such as nearsightedness, farsightedness, and astigmatism), strabismus (eye misalignment), and presbyopia (difficulty reading close-up). Regular ophthalmological examinations are essential.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Individuals with KBG syndrome may exhibit eczema-like skin conditions, including dry, itchy patches that can be stubborn to treat. Skin care routines and gentle skincare products are recommended.

## 9) DENTAL

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Dental issues in KBG syndrome include weak enamel, susceptibility to tooth decay, and the aforementioned brachydactyly (shortened fingers). Regular dental check-ups and thorough home-care routines are vital.

## 10) EDUCATION

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Academic performance in children with KBG syndrome can vary widely. While many achieve success in mainstream education, those with more significant learning challenges may require additional support in the classroom. An Individualized Education Plan (IEP) tailored to their unique needs is beneficial.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Behavioural and developmental differences are frequent in KBG syndrome. Features include autism spectrum disorder (ASD), attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), and anxiety. Early identification and appropriate interventions can improve outcomes.

## 12) SKELETAL

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Skeletal concerns in KBG syndrome include brachydactyly (shortened fingers) and an increased incidence of skeletal anomalies such as scoliosis and hip dysplasia. Orthodontic and orthopedic assessments are advisable.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
Recommendations for screening and treatments based on the presented symptoms:

1. **Orthodontics**: Given the presence of brachydactyly, orthodontic evaluation and possible corrective procedures should be considered.
   
2. **Pediatric Dentistry**: Frequent dental check-ups are essential to monitor and address issues such as cavities and gum disease.

3. **Physical Therapy**: To address coordination and balance issues, physical therapy sessions should be incorporated into the routine.

4. **Occupational Therapy**: To aid in fine motor skill development and assist with activities of daily living.

5. **Speech Therapy**: Considering the reported speech delay, speech therapy might provide benefits.

6. **Behavioral Support**: Given the behavioral differences noted, support programs targeting autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and ADHD may offer relief.

7. **Vaccinations**: Routine vaccinations should be administered according to standard protocols, given the increased likelihood of autoimmune reactions.

8. **Prophylactic Antibiotics**: For recurrent ear infections, prophylactic antibiotics may be warranted.

9. **Regular Medical Review**: Annual comprehensive health reviews should be conducted to monitor for any emerging medical concerns.

This targeted approach aims to mitigate the various challenges faced by children with KBG syndrome, ensuring they receive the best possible care throughout their lives.

Parent: Our son often squints when trying to focus on things, which makes us worry about his eyesight. It's not just when reading or watching TV; it happens even when he's playing or looking at pictures.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: We've noticed he seems to pick up on some sounds but completely misses others, even when they're pretty loud. It's like he's filtering out certain frequencies or something. We're not sure what's going on, but it's definitely affected his ability to follow conversations sometimes.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: His teeth are very prone to breaking or chipping. We have to be super careful with what he eats and make sure he brushes them gently but thoroughly. It's been a challenge since he was little, and we're always on the lookout for any signs of tooth decay or damage.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: Yes, there's a structural issue with his heart that the cardiologist keeps an eye on. We go for regular check-ups to monitor it closely. So far, it hasn't held him back from playing or running around with his friends, but we do have to keep it in mind when considering physical activities.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's hormones.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: He experiences seizures. They can be scary, but we've learned how to manage them better over time. His neurologist is great and helps us adjust his medication as needed.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding, stomach, bowel).
Parent: When he was a baby, feeding was a real challenge. He had trouble latching on and would get frustrated easily. Thankfully, that phase passed, and now he eats fairly normally.

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: Besides the heart condition and seizures, our main concern now is his scoliosis. It affects his posture and can cause back pain if not managed properly. Additionally, he struggles to express himself clearly; it's hard for him to find the right words or explain what he wants or needs. We're working on that with speech therapy.
